items.title: AFC Toronto beats Montreal Roses to win 1st NSL title
items.summary_auto: Olivia Chisholm's first half goal allowed AFC Toronto to capture their first Diana B. Matheson Cup with a 1-0 victory over the Montreal Roses Saturday afternoon at TD Place in Ottawa.

items.title: A 5th soldier injured in CFB Wainwright fire has died, officials say
items.summary_auto: A fifth soldier, Pte. William Douglas Dal Bianco, has died as a result of the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, the Department of National Defence says.

items.title: New Orleans port sues for control of China-linked tanker that crashed into cruise ship
items.summary_auto: Just hours after a tanker in New Orleans lost its steering and slammed into a docked river cruise boat, the city's port sued to make sure federal investigators can seize the vessel that is owned by a subsidiary of a Chinese company.

items.title: European security plan floated by U.S. would benefit Putin, Zelenskyy says
items.summary_auto: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the United States had raised the possibility of a new security framework for Europe as part of efforts to end Russia’s war in Ukraine, warning that Moscow could use such discussions to weaken NATO and reshape the continent’s borders.

items.title: Gorgeous, heartrending Club Kid is hitting Canadian theatres. Read our TIFF review
items.summary_auto: Hitting Canadian theatres now, Club Kid is without doubt a major work. It was without doubt one of the best films at this year's Toronto International Film Festival. And while there is some doubt here, Club Kid just might make you cry.

items.title: SpaceX Starship re-enters Earth, lands at same spot from which it launched a day ago
items.summary_auto: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft on Saturday returned from its longest flight in orbit yet to the Texas launch tower it was launched from a day prior, demonstrating the first key recovery of the rocket system's centerpiece vessel in the company's decade-long effort to ‌develop a fully reusable rocket.

items.title: Carney says he will not boycott APEC 'family photo' with Putin
items.summary_auto: Prime Minister Mark Carney says he will participate in an upcoming group photo with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit out of respect for the host, Chinese President Xi Jinping.

items.title: Margaret Atwood joins other bird lovers to fight against a proposed 600-foot tower on Pelee Island
items.summary_auto: Atwood called the location, which is one road over from the new Atwood-Gibson Bird Centre, "one of the stupidest places on the planet" to put a tower.

items.title: Change to Ontario's 'safer-supply' opioid prescriptions abruptly paused due to legal challenge
items.summary_auto: A controversial change to "safer-supply" opioid prescriptions in Ontario that would force recipients to take them in front of a pharmacist, rather than on their own schedule at home, has been abruptly paused due to a legal challenge. Critics said the proposal would drastically affect the lives of drug users while causing potential chaos at pharmacies.

items.title: 3 kids, 2 adults in life-threatening condition after Burlington, Ont., house fire: police
items.summary_auto: Five people, including three children, are in life-threatening condition in hospital after a house fire in Burlington on Saturday morning, Halton police say.

items.title: Vancouver duo's song goes viral after featuring in Grand Theft Auto VI
items.summary_auto: Bob Moses didn’t have to steal a car, pull off a heist, or even pick up a controller to score big with Grand Theft Auto VI. All the Vancouver-based electronic duo needed was a killer song and an email from Rockstar Games.

items.title: Why is Alberta ditching diversity, equity and inclusion in hiring practices?
items.summary_auto: Are hiring policies that strive for workplace diversity actually a problem that needs solving? Or is the UCP government engaging in political posturing? Panelists who spoke to CBC's West of Centre are split on the answer.

items.title: Microsoft services fully restored after global outage
items.summary_auto: Microsoft said on Saturday that services had fully recovered across Teams, Outlook and its other products, ending a global outage that crippled online communications ‌for businesses and governments for over 24 hours.

items.title: New bridge in Prince George park is for frogs and other tiny critters
items.summary_auto: A new bridge above an amphibian migration trail in a Prince George city park is expected to give tiny salamanders, frogs and toads a fighting chance at survival each summer.

items.title: Scam targeting minor hockey teams 'heartbreaking' for affected kids
items.summary_auto: Valerie Favreau, the chair of the Oromocto Minor Hockey Association, said two under-13 teams signed up for a tournament in Stanley, with each team losing around $750 in fake registration fees. It's a type of scam that is referred to as "spear phishing," according to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.

items.title: Snowbirds set to fly iconic jets for last time this weekend
items.summary_auto: Fifty-five years after the team's formation, the Canadian Forces Snowbirds' iconic jets will grace the skies one last time. The aerobatics team's CT-114 Tutor jets are set to fly over Calgary's McMahon Stadium on Sunday as part of the 113th Grey Cup festivities, before being grounded permanently.

items.title: People called this Elora, Ont., company for a washer it supposedly sells. Except it doesn't even make washers
items.summary_auto: This week, hundreds of people were making calls and sending emails and messages to an Elora, Ont., appliance maker wanting to buy their so-called revolutionary washing machine, the "Keel." The problem? Elora's Stirling Marathon doesn't even make washers. The company is a victim of a scam Youtube video generated with artificial intelligence that has since been taken down.

items.title: Ford government spent nearly $46M on 2 ad campaigns, FOI docs reveal
items.summary_auto: The Ford government spent nearly $46 million on two ad campaigns that ran across various social media and video platforms over the course of the 2025-26 year, records obtained by the CBC through a freedom-of-information request show.

items.title: These farmers are worried N.L. is facing another hay shortage
items.summary_auto: Farmers and livestock owners are once again at risk of running out of hay following a disastrous shortage last year, according to some farmers. Demand for hay is growing each year and production can’t keep up, says the owners of 3C Farms in Comfort Cove-Newstead.

items.title: 4 decades ago, Robert Munsch attended Moira Green's birthday. Her story became a children's classic
items.summary_auto: Four decades ago, Robert Munsch flew to the Northwest Territories in search of inspiration. The beloved author found it at Moira Green's sixth birthday party.

items.title: Trump's attempts to intimidate the International Criminal Court are 'futile,' says Canadian judge
items.summary_auto: Kimberly Prost, a Canadian judge at the International Criminal Court, was sanctioned by the Trump administration last August. Despite impacts including cancelled credit cards and frozen bank accounts, she says attempts to intimidate her and other court officials are 'futile.'

items.title: Quebec assumes parents help pay for post-secondary schooling. Students say many can't
items.summary_auto: Thousands of post-secondary and university students held strikes across Quebec this week to denounce “austerity measures and growing precariousness” among students in the face of the rising cost of living and the provincewide housing crisis. Among other things, the coalition is calling for a reform of Quebec's student financial aid program.

items.title: Minimum wage hasn't kept pace with the cost of living across Canada, new reports show
items.summary_auto: Of the 59 cities and regions in reports for every province reviewed by CBC News, none had a provincial minimum wage equal to the calculated living wage — the amount a full-time worker needs to meet their basic needs, manage unexpected expenses and participate meaningfully in their community.

items.title: Montreal's deteriorating Dieppe Park to get $35M makeover — but not any time soon
items.summary_auto: Montreal is planning a $35-million makeover for Dieppe Park, including replacing its crumbling riverfront retaining wall. But surfers, fishermen and visitors will have to wait until 2029 for work to begin, and even that tentative date depends on further planning and environmental approvals.

items.title: Canadian judge decries U.S. sanctions of International Criminal Court as 'attack in favour of impunity'
items.summary_auto: Kimberly Prost, a Canadian judge at the International Criminal Court, was sanctioned by the Trump administration last August. Despite impacts including cancelled credit cards and frozen bank accounts, she says attempts to intimidate her and other court officials are 'futile.'

items.title: Is a cure on the horizon for hepatitis B? New drug offers hope, but there's a 'long way to go'
items.summary_auto: Is a cure on the horizon for hepatitis B? A newly-approved drug offers hope, but wiping out this viral liver infection remains a challenge.

items.title: Canada's Dabrowski, Brazil's Stefani advance to semifinals at WTA Finals after perfect group stage
items.summary_auto: Ottawa’s Gabriela Dabrowski and Brazil’s Luisa Stefani advanced to the doubles semifinals at the WTA Finals after defeating Latvia’s Jelena Ostapenko and Taiwan’s Su-Wei Hsieh 2-6, 7-6 (2), 10-3 on Friday in Indian Wells, Calif.

items.title: Premier says Manitoba nearing limits of what it can do on affordability, so he's going after big corporations
items.summary_auto: Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew says the provincial government is reaching the limits of what it can do to ease the cost of living without sacrificing the revenue needed to fund public services, and that corporate giants need to do their part.

items.title: Sentencing delayed for Edmonton man who left beaten girlfriend to drown, believing she was already dead
items.summary_auto: WARNING: This story contains distressing and graphic details.

items.title: COVID-19 school disruptions still impacting students today, learning loss report finds
items.summary_auto: A new report says Canadian students are still feeling the impact of the COVID pandemic's massive upset to their schooling, with declining achievement — particularly in math — and a discrepancy between standardized test scores and the grades kids receive in class.

items.title: UN hails progress in Ebola response, cites insecurity as biggest challenge
items.summary_auto: UN health officials on Friday hailed progress in the Ebola response six months after the ​outbreak first prompted global concerns, but cautioned that ‌the disease continues to spread to more remote and dangerous parts of Congo.

items.title: 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski testifies he was beaten, tortured during alleged kidnapping
items.summary_auto: Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski described being beaten with a gun and tortured with knives and a lighter in the back of a truck as he began his testimony at the trial of his alleged kidnappers Friday in Toronto.

items.title: Spanish goalkeeper barred 12 games for collision leading to death of Tenerife striker
items.summary_auto: While Spain mourns the death of a soccer player who suffered a cardiac arrest after an on-field collision, the emergency medical treatment he received is falling under scrutiny.
